root_cause_hypothesis:
Scored outcome is a clean PASS (build 1 / bp_clean 1 / golden_match 1), but the run needed two extra build cycles, both caused by the same gap in get_knowledge(topic="lookups").
KNOWLEDGE_GAP 1 (cost 2 builds): the topic teaches the reference-control override as _control.registerOverrideMethod(methodStr(FormReferenceControl, lookupReference), ...) without saying which X++ TYPE the control variable must have. xppc rejects both obvious readings:
  build 1: ClassDoesNotContainMethod: Class FormReferenceControl does not contain a definition for method registerOverrideMethod
  build 2: ClassDoesNotContainMethod: Class FormControl does not contain a definition for method registerOverrideMethod
  Verified fact: registerOverrideMethod is declared on the CONCRETE control class (FormStringControl compiled first try), NOT on FormControl and NOT on FormReferenceControl. The design control behind an AxFormReferenceGroupControl child is an AxFormStringControl, so the variable is a FormStringControl; only the HANDLER parameter is typed FormReferenceControl. The topic should state this, otherwise every agent following it burns 2 build cycles.
KNOWLEDGE_GAP 2 (cosmetic): the topic claims addLookupMethod is something "which SysTableLookup does not have". get_object_info shows addLookupMethod(str,boolean) inherited from SysTableLookupBase on BOTH SysTableLookup and SysReferenceTableLookup. The claim is false; the real reference-only difference is the newParameters argument-2 type.
TOOL_DEFECT 1: get_object_info(objectType="form", options={searchControl:"..."}) is IGNORED. Verified with an EXACT existing control name (form CustGroup, searchControl "Grid_TaxGroupId") and with a prefix ("Grid_"): both returned the full control tree, byte-identical to the unfiltered call. The tool then advises "Use searchControl to jump straight to one control" in its own truncation message. Consequence: form CustTable (635 controls) blew the token cap and had to be dumped to a file and grepped — exactly the workaround the tool exists to prevent.
TOOL_DEFECT 2 (minor): get_object_info(objectType="class", options={include:"xml"}) failed with "no file on disk" for CustFreeInvoice_AppSuite_Tax_BR_Extension although find_references had just returned its absolute path; it only resolved after options.modelName="Foundation" was added. Model resolution for include:"xml" should fall back to the index path.
TOOL_DEFECT 3 (minor, self-healing): d365fo_file modify/replace-code — the C# bridge rejected 2 of 4 replacements with "oldCode not found" while the same oldCode WAS present; the server XML-writer fallback applied them correctly. Bridge-side oldCode matching appears to normalise whitespace differently from the writer.
VALIDATOR_GAP: validate_code(mode="references") flags kernel classes used as methodStr intrinsic targets as ERRORS, while flagging the SAME class in a type declaration as a WARNING with an explicit "if it is a kernel class this is a false positive" hint. Same root cause as the known kernel-enum gap; the intrinsic-target rule should inherit the same kernel-name allowlist/downgrade.
CASE-DEFINITION NOTE: the case id says "multiselect" but neither the instruction (three numbered requirements) nor the tags mention SysLookupMultiSelectCtrl. The golden deliberately omits it: a multi-select writes a comma list through an unbound control and there is no coherent place for it on a standard form extension (its real home is a SysOperation UIBuilder dialog). Either drop "multiselect" from the id or move it to a dialog-based case.
